Full sequence 50 -> 49.5 (7/3) -> 49.0 -> 48.5 -> 48.0 -> 47.5. DISAMBIGUATION, ruled and NOT retuned: my criterion excluded 'a scheduled draft step-down'. Reading 'scheduled' as 'announced in advance with a date' would make the criterion UNFIREABLE, since every ACP restriction is announced with an effective date -- that reading is the dead-gate class I audited seven of on 8/21. 'Scheduled' therefore means ROUTINE/CALENDAR-DRIVEN, and the distinguishing features are DIRECTION and DRIVER: ACP's routine seasonal adjustments are draft INCREASES tied to the rainy season, while this is a five-step REDUCTION sequence ACP itself attributes to hydrology and El Nino. FIRES. FIRE DATE IS A FLOOR, NOT AN EXACT: the sequence began 7/3 at 49.5 ft, which implies an EARLIER advisory I have not retrieved, so the true first fire is likely late June. Dated to the earliest I can evidence at primary. WHY I MISSED IT FOR 51 DAYS -- the instrument, not inattention: limb (b) is transits <=32/day, and ACP states explicitly 'The draft adjustment will not affect the number of daily vessel transits.' MY REGISTERED BAND MEASURES THE VARIABLE ACP IS DELIBERATELY HOLDING CONSTANT. Transits are structurally blind to a draft-only restriction by the issuer's own design. Limb (a) existed and would have caught it, but I checked the cheap limb and my 8/13 STATUS logged this very sequence as a 'scheduled step-down' with 'no binding restriction'. OPEN GAP: Gatun Lake ELEVATION -- the actual physical driver -- is held nowhere in my tree; ACP's own dashboard is TLS-broken AND JS-rendered. No secondary substituted.

LOWERED 70%->55% on 2026-08-21. TWO INDEPENDENT PIECES OF EVIDENCE ARRIVED AGAINST THE PREMISE, BOTH FROM THE ISSUING AUTHORITIES THEMSELVES. (1) NIFC's 8/01 outlook attributes the southern-Plains dryness TO El Nino -- 'a common theme in summers with intensifying El Nino conditions' -- and forecasts above-normal potential to DEVELOP through large parts of Oklahoma and Texas, with potential to carry into September. AEO-09 predicts a historic El Nino REMOVES that potential; NIFC is currently using El Nino to EXPLAIN it. The two are reconcilable -- El Nino's southern-tier WET signal is a COLD-SEASON teleconnection while its late-summer effect on the southern Plains runs the other way -- but the prediction as written did not distinguish them, and that conflation was mine. (2) CPC's 8/20 seasonal discussion (primary) explicitly forecasts a DELAYED ONSET: 'the closest natural analogs to the current EP-based El Nino are suggestive of a delayed onset of the robust cold season wet signal across the southern tier', with above-normal precipitation chances only 'modest (generally 33 to 50 percent)' across the southern tier and Southern Plains during OND, ramping up 'deeper into the cold season' and 'especially late winter.' The deadline here is 12/01, so the mechanism is now forecast to arrive largely AFTER the window closes. COUNTERWEIGHT, which is why this is 55% and not lower: the same 8/01 NIFC outlook ALREADY returns much of the Southern Area to normal in its September panel, so a HIT on the 9/1 or 10/1 outlook remains entirely live. FALSIFIER unchanged in kind but now dated: if the 9/1 and 10/1 outlooks both keep TX/OK above-normal in their current-month panel, this goes to <=30% and I stop defending it.

Criteria verbatim: '>=1 EEA2+ posting OR 202(c) order in PJM footprint by 9/7'. WHAT SATISFIES IT: DOE Order No. 202-26-41, issued 2026-09-01 to PJM Interconnection L.L.C. under FPA s202(c), effective 2026-09-01 through 11:59 PM ET 2026-09-08 - 'directs PJM to dispatch specified units and to order their operation as needed to maintain reliability' and 'authorizes PJM to direct backup generation resources to operate as a last resort before declaring an Energy Emergency Alert (EEA) 3 or during an EEA 3'. VERIFIED AT TWO INDEPENDENT PRIMARIES: (1) DOE CESER 2026 202(c) order index (energy.gov/ceser/2026-doe-202c-orders); (2) PJM Inside Lines 'Hot Weather Operations Update - Sept. 2, 2026', verbatim: 'PJM requested and received a combined emergency order... to be effective through Sept. 8, from the U.S. Department of Energy for temporary relief from environmental permit restrictions for generating units and/or to direct backup generation resources at large loads to operate'. THE POSTING LIMB DID NOT FIRE: PJM posted NERC EEA-1 twice (#105473 9/1 18:03, #105479 9/2 16:00) plus a Pre-Emergency Load Management Reduction Action (#105472, 9/1 17:15, AEP BGE COMED DOM PEPCO). EEA-1 IS NOT EEA2+. The disjunction needed only one limb; the 202(c) limb carried it. Recording BOTH facts so the grade is not later misread as an EEA2 event. *** IT WAS ALREADY A HIT ON 2026-07-14 AND I MISSED IT FOR SEVEN WEEKS. *** DOE Order No. 202-26-35 (issued 7/14, PJM, effective 7/14-7/21, 'dispatch units for reliability; backup generation at loads before/during EEA 3') ALSO satisfies the criteria and post-dates this prediction's 7/10 registration. On 7/22 I wrote 'the 7/15-16 EEA-1 is sub-EEA2 (near-miss, not banked)' - a CORRECT statement about the posting limb, applied as if it settled the whole prediction. The DOE order covering that same heat episode was one index page away and I never checked it, at any of four subsequent boots. ROOT CAUSE IS DOCUMENTATION, NOT RESEARCH: this registered row always carried both limbs. Every carry-forward SUMMARY of it dropped the second - STATUS said 'WATT-02 (9/7) - EEA2+ by Labor Day'; SCRATCH said 'its bar is a POSTING'; and the 2026-09-02 PROME task brief inherited that compression and restated it back to me as established fact ('its bar is a POSTING, not a price spike (your own note)'). FOUR derived surfaces carried a one-limb rule; the ledger was correct throughout. => GRADE AT THE REGISTERED ROW, NEVER AT THE SURFACE THAT QUOTES IT. NOTE THE MIGRATION: the compressed caveat is TRUE of the NEIGHBOURING prediction - WATT-06's criteria really is posting-only ('a Max Gen Emergency / Load Management Alert (EEA-1) or above, PJM-RTO region, effective 7/17-8/15, on emergencyprocedures.pjm.com'). A correct caveat migrated to the wrong prediction. WATT-06's MISS is UNAFFECTED and stands: 202-26-35 was issued 7/14, outside WATT-06's 7/17-8/15 window, and WATT-06's bar is a PJM posting, not a DOE order. registered if_falsified DOES NOT EXECUTE (it was written for a MISS). CONTENT OF THE HIT: the recurrence case is now n=3 episodes in one season - 7/3 (EEA2 + 202-26-32A/33A), 7/15-16 (EEA-1 + 202-26-35), 9/1-9/3+ (EEA-1 x2 + 202-26-41 + a dispatched load-management action) - and it SPANS JULY AND SEPTEMBER, so the 'heat-clustered, not a structural cadence' read that WATT-06's MISS correctly established FOR JULY does not extend across the season. A SUCCESSOR IS OWED once the current episode closes; deliberately NOT registered mid-episode.

If FALSIFIED (a qualifying EEA-class posting or a new 202(c) order in the window): the falsification is graded FIRST and explained SECOND, and the explanation is NOT automatic. STEP 1 - GRADE: WATT-11 is a MISS. Unconditional. A heat-driven event is still a MISS; there is no weather exemption. STEP 2 - CLASSIFY, then investigate: (a) HEAT-DRIVEN (a late heat dome, confirmed with AEOLUS) => MISS on the count, but the heat-coupled mechanism is NOT falsified - record both, and do NOT let the second soften the first. (b) NON-HEAT => MISS, and it OPENS AN INVESTIGATION - it does NOT by itself establish reserve-margin erosion. Reserve margin is ONE candidate among several and must WIN against the others before any score moves: a large forced-outage cluster, a transmission/contingency event, and a fuel-supply event must each be eliminated. Instrument: the DM2 generation-outage series, same method as the 8/16 forced-outage z-test (KB-WATT-089). ONLY IF reserve-margin erosion survives that elimination: escalate to P2 (structural), +conf on WATT-08's Door-B direction, and re-open the P1 seasonal-dormancy framing.
